title: Sunny Australia
subtitle: Impressions of the Country and People
summary: Archibald Marshall (1866–1934), an English novelist, went to Australia in the late summer of 1909 as Special Commissioner of the Daily Mail and stayed until February 1910, travelling through all six states. Part I, “Recollections”, is a personal account of the journey: Sydney and its society, the Governors, stations in New South Wales and Queensland, Melbourne and the Western District, Adelaide and the wine districts, Tasmania, Perth, and Kalgoorlie. Part II, “Impressions”, is made from his articles for the paper, on subjects such as a home station, sugar, the bushranger, the Barren Jack dam, dairying, sheep shearing, irrigation at Mildura, orcharding, Port Arthur, wheat, vineyards, and timber. Sir George Reid, then High Commissioner, wrote the preface. The book has 32 photographs.
omitted_from_reading: The half-title, the printed contents, and the list of illustrations are in the JSON only.
notes_on_text: Part I is printed as twenty numbered sections without titles; here each is a page of its own, with a title of the editor’s in the contents.
The leaves of tissue paper before the title page, through which the title and frontispiece show, are left out.
